about: The decisions a design system has to answer, so that coverage can be measured instead of claimed. A repository's ledger (design/decisions.yaml) reuses these ids and may add its own. `layer` is the artifact a decision constrains: the thing you would have to change to break it. `sources` says where the question was seen: a decision seen in two or more is core, the rest are candidates. `tier` overrides the tier of its layer. `note` marks a decision that could sit elsewhere.

sources.reference-ledger: A working ledger of 50 decisions in one of the owner's product repositories, read 2026-11-12.
sources.component-audit: The owner's audit of 49 design-system components in another product repository, and the target table of the architecture note, 2026-11-09.
sources.repo-standards-floor: What the design floor of repo-setup decides, generates or checks.
sources.design-assembly: What this plugin decides and checks today.

decisions.question: Is the product an application people work in, or a content site people read?
Which accessibility conformance level does the product commit to?
decisions.note: In the reference ledger it is recorded as the source of wcag-aa, not as a row of its own.

decisions.question: What is the main task of each screen?
decisions.note: Decided per screen, so it belongs with templates, not with foundations.

decisions.question: In what order does each screen present its information?
decisions.note: Decided per screen, so it belongs with templates, not with foundations.

decisions.question: What do the words on each screen say?
decisions.note: Decided per screen, so it belongs with templates, not with foundations.

decisions.question: Which source color does the theme start from?
Does the source use color roles only, never a raw colour?
Which palette may neutral and status colours come from?
Does every pair of color roles reach the contrast ratio of the conformance level?
Is the tonal palette exactly what the source color gives?
Does the source use the type scale only, never an arbitrary size?
Are the sizes and line heights of the type scale the decided ones?
Does the source use the spacing scale only, never an arbitrary distance?
Is the unit of the spacing scale the decided one?
Does the source use the shape scale only, never an arbitrary corner radius?
Is the corner radius the decided step of the shape scale?
Which durations and easings may motion use?
Which modes does the theme have: light, dark?
Which status tones exist, and what colour does each take?
Which brand values depart from the standard palette, and where are they listed?
decisions.note: Could sit in governance: it is a list of exceptions.

decisions.question: Does the source use the core components only, never a raw control?
Does every table go through the system's table component?
Does every dialog go through the system's dialog component?
How does a component render as another element?
Which icon set is used, at which sizes and stroke?
Is a component's look changed only through its variants?
Is inline style forbidden?
Are class names written whole, so that tools can read them?
How is a component's size on the atoms-to-organisms scale determined?
Which column type does each data field have?
decisions.note: Could sit in content: it decides formatting as well as the cell component.

decisions.question: How does a column type decide alignment?
How is a column's width computed?
When is a table dense?
Does every control reach the target size of the conformance level?
decisions.note: Could sit in foundations: a size token can carry it.

decisions.question: Which states does a view have, and what does each show: loading state, empty state, error state?
Through which single channel is the person notified?
How does a record open beside a list?
How does a cell that cannot be edited show it?
Which cells are edited in place?
When does a destructive action ask first, and when does it offer undo?
What feedback does a wait of each length get?
Can a login code be pasted?
How do search, filters and paging behave on a list?
Where does every label on a screen come from?
Which words must not be swapped for one another?
Which label wins when more than one source names a thing?
Which voice and tone does each kind of message take?
What are the parts of an error sentence?
Are numbers, money and dates formatted in one place, for the product's localization?
Does every page have exactly one main region and one top heading?
Does every page fit its width at every tested screen size?
Does every page pass the automated accessibility checks?
decisions.note: A page-level check; the conformance level it tests against is conformance-level.

decisions.question: At which screen sizes are pages checked?
Is the focused element never hidden by another?
How does navigation change on a small screen?
Which loading and responsiveness thresholds must pages meet?
Which page layouts exist?
Which real screen is the reference implementation of each template?
Does every exception to a design lint rule carry a reason?
Do the design checks run in the repository's gate, in a way that can fail?
Which part of the system may import which?
Through which entry points may a module be used?
Which product rules may no screen break?
Does every escape name the layer that should have caught it?
